title: Coordination Compounds: The Chemistry of Metal Complexes

questions.question: In the complex [Co(NH3)6]Cl3, the coordination number of cobalt and the oxidation state of cobalt are respectively:
questions.rationale: Six ammine ligands surround the metal, so the coordination number is 6 (octahedral). The complex cation carries a +3 charge with neutral NH3 ligands, so cobalt is in the +3 oxidation state.

questions.question: How many ions per formula unit does CoCl3·5NH3, i.e. [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2, give in aqueous solution?
questions.rationale: The complex ion [Co(NH3)5Cl](2+) is a single entity; only the two outer chlorides ionise. Total particles: 1 complex cation + 2 chloride anions = 3 ions. Werner verified this by precipitating only 2 of the 3 chlorides with AgNO3.

questions.question: EDTA(4-) is classified as which type of ligand?
questions.rationale: EDTA4- donates through six donor atoms (two nitrogens and four carboxylate oxygens), wrapping the metal like a claw. This hexadentate chelation is why EDTA complexes are exceptionally stable.

questions.question: The IUPAC name of K4[Fe(CN)6] is:
questions.rationale: Cation first (potassium), then the anionic complex with ligand names ending in -ido (hexacyanido), and an anionic metal takes the -ate suffix with its oxidation state: ferrate(II). Hence potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II).

questions.question: Which pair represents ionisation isomers?
questions.rationale: Ionisation isomers swap a ligand between the inner sphere and the ionisable counter-ion position: one releases Br- and the other releases SO4(2-) with AgNO3 or BaCl2 tests. Same overall formula, different ions in solution.

questions.question: [Ni(CO)4], [Ni(CN)4]2-, and [NiCl4]2- respectively show which geometries?
questions.rationale: Ni(CO)4 uses sp3 hybrids (tetrahedral, zero-valent nickel). Strong-field CN- pairs the electrons into dsp2 hybrids for square planar [Ni(CN)4]2-. Weak-field Cl- leaves sp3 tetrahedral [NiCl4]2- — magnetic and spectral data confirm all three.

questions.question: Which ligand produces the LARGEST crystal field splitting in an octahedral complex?
questions.rationale: The spectrochemical series places CN- (and CO) at the strong-field extreme, well beyond NH3, H2O and the weak halides. Larger splitting means low-spin configurations and strong d-d absorption shifted to shorter wavelengths.

questions.question: A d6 metal ion in a weak octahedral field has how many unpaired electrons?
questions.rationale: Weak field means small splitting, so electrons occupy all five d orbitals before pairing (high spin): t2g holds 4 electrons (one pair + two singles) and eg holds 2 singles, giving 4 unpaired electrons and strong paramagnetism.

questions.question: Why are complexes of d0 and d10 metal ions usually colourless?
questions.rationale: Colour in complexes arises from d-d transitions across the crystal-field gap. With an empty (d0) or completely filled (d10) d set there is no vacant destination for the electron, so no visible absorption and no colour — as in Zn2+ and Sc3+ salts.

questions.question: Carbon monoxide poisoning occurs because CO bound to haemoglobin's Fe(II):
options: Binds about 200 times more strongly than oxygen and blocks O2 transport
Chelates through both C and O atoms
questions.rationale: CO is a strong-field ligand forming a very stable carbonyl-type bond with the haem iron, outcompeting oxygen roughly 200:1. The blocked sites can no longer carry O2, causing oxygen starvation — the core of CO toxicity.
